name: Tara Iti Golf Club
description: A Tom Doak masterpiece ranked number one in New Zealand and consistently placed inside the world's top 20. This invitation-only links course threads through pristine coastal dunes north of Auckland, delivering a raw, strategic test of golf in an untouched landscape.

name: Cape Kidnappers Golf Course
description: A world Top 100 clifftop masterpiece designed by Tom Doak, featuring a dramatic ridge-and-valley layout high above Hawke's Bay. Stunning ocean views, bold bunkering, and unforgettable par threes make it one of the most spectacular golf experiences on the planet.

name: Te Arai Links South
description: Designed by the acclaimed duo of Coore and Crenshaw, this coastal links sits between native forest and the Tasman Sea. Ranked second in New Zealand, the course flows through dramatic duneland with wide strategic corridors and firm, fast playing surfaces.

name: Kauri Cliffs Golf Course
description: A World Top 100 clifftop course designed by David Harman, with 15 of its 18 holes offering sweeping views over the Pacific Ocean. Set on a luxury lodge estate in the Bay of Islands, Kauri Cliffs combines breathtaking scenery with championship-calibre golf.

name: Te Arai Links North
description: Tom Doak's North course at Te Arai weaves through a striking corridor of coastal forest and open duneland. The layout journeys from the coast into the trees and back again, offering a quieter, more contemplative companion to its celebrated neighbour.

name: Jack's Point Golf Club
description: Spectacular lakeside links set between the jagged Remarkables mountain range and the shores of Lake Wakatipu. Consistently ranked among the top five courses in New Zealand, the layout delivers dramatic elevation changes and panoramic alpine scenery on virtually every hole.

name: The Hills Golf Club
description: An exclusive private course built on a former deer farm in the Arrowtown hills, known for its large-scale outdoor sculptures scattered across the property. The Hills has hosted the NZ PGA Championship and attracts some of the country's strongest tournament fields.

name: Kinloch Club
description: New Zealand's only Jack Nicklaus Signature Course, laid out over dramatic volcanic terrain beside Lake Taupo. The links-style design, strategic bunkering, and stunning lake and mountain views have earned Kinloch a place among the country's finest courses.

name: Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club
description: Host of the New Zealand Open twelve times, this Alex Russell-designed links is widely regarded as one of the finest in the Southern Hemisphere. Modelled on the great British links, the course features rolling dunes, firm fairways, and challenging seaside conditions along the Kapiti Coast. It consistently ranks among New Zealand's top courses.

name: Titirangi Golf Club
description: New Zealand's only course designed by the legendary Alister MacKenzie, architect of Augusta National and Royal Melbourne. Founded in 1909, the classic parkland layout winds through native bush in Auckland's Waitakere Ranges, and remains one of the country's most revered golfing experiences.

name: Royal Auckland & Grange Golf Club
description: One of New Zealand's most historic and prestigious clubs, founded in 1894. The private 36-hole facility in central Auckland has hosted countless national championships and continues to set the standard for course conditioning and tradition in New Zealand golf.

name: Millbrook Resort (Coronet)
description: Designed by Sir Bob Charles, New Zealand's only major championship winner, this alpine resort course has served as a regular host of the New Zealand Open. The Coronet nine at Millbrook weaves through mature trees and water features against a stunning mountain backdrop.

name: Millbrook Resort (Remarkables)
description: The newer nine at Millbrook Resort, offering wide fairways framed by spectacular views of the Remarkables mountain range. Together with the Coronet nine, it completes one of the most scenic 18-hole resort experiences in the South Island.

name: Royal Wellington Golf Club
description: Wellington's premier private club, set beside the Hutt River with a championship parkland layout that has hosted numerous national tournaments. The mature, tree-lined course offers a demanding yet fair test of golf in a beautiful setting, with the Rimutaka Range providing a dramatic backdrop.

name: Wairakei Golf + Sanctuary
description: A world-class course set inside a predator-free wildlife sanctuary near Taupo, where native birds roam freely across the fairways. Ranked in the top 20 in New Zealand, it offers a rare combination of championship golf and conservation in a truly unique setting.

name: Christchurch Golf Club
description: A premier Canterbury club ranked in the top 20 in New Zealand, recently upgraded to deliver a quasi-links feel. The course combines strategic bunkering with excellent conditioning, making it one of the finest tests of golf in the South Island.

name: Clearwater Golf Club
description: A premium resort course on a lake near Christchurch airport, designed to international standards. The water features, mature plantings, and mountain backdrop create a stunning setting for a challenging and memorable round.

name: Carrington Golf Club
description: A scenic resort course perched on the Karikari Peninsula in the Far North, featuring panoramic ocean views and the longest par 5 in New Zealand at 569 metres. The dramatic coastal setting and warm subtropical climate make it a memorable round year-round.

name: Arrowtown Golf Club
description: A charming course threaded through the valleys below the historic gold-mining town of Arrowtown. Mature deciduous trees line the fairways, making autumn rounds particularly memorable, and the relaxed atmosphere suits golfers of all abilities.

name: Formosa Golf Resort
description: A scenic resort course on the Pohutukawa Coast east of Auckland, surrounded by native bush and rolling countryside. The well-presented layout makes for an enjoyable day out, especially during summer when the namesake pohutukawa trees are in full crimson bloom.

name: Queenstown Golf Club
description: Set on the Kelvin Heights peninsula, this course is surrounded on three sides by Lake Wakatipu with sweeping views of the Remarkables, Cecil Peak, and Walter Peak. It is one of the most photographed golf settings in New Zealand.

name: Wanaka Golf Club
description: A scenic parkland layout beside Lake Wanaka with views stretching to the snow-capped peaks of Mt Aspiring National Park. The course suits all levels and provides a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere in one of the South Island's most popular lakeside towns.

name: Boulcott Farm Heritage Golf Club
description: A well-regarded parkland course in the Hutt Valley, built on the site of a historic colonial farm. The layout features mature trees, gentle undulations, and the Hutt River as a natural boundary, creating an attractive and challenging round close to Wellington.

name: Dunedin Golf Club (Balmacewen)
description: Dunedin's premier private club, Balmacewen features a well-maintained parkland layout with tree-lined fairways on gently rolling terrain. It is one of the strongest clubs in the Otago region and has hosted numerous provincial championships.

name: Muriwai Golf Club
description: A rugged links course perched beside the famous Muriwai gannet colony and black sand beach on Auckland's wild west coast. Exposed to the Tasman Sea winds, it offers a raw, links-style challenge that feels worlds away from the city.

name: Remuera Golf Club
description: A well-regarded private members' club in the leafy Auckland suburb of Remuera. Mature trees and immaculate presentation make this parkland course one of the most pleasant rounds in the city.

name: Russley Golf Club
description: A quality Christchurch parkland club conveniently located near the airport. The well-established tree-lined fairways and manicured greens provide an excellent test of golf in a mature, attractive setting.

name: Rotorua Golf Club (Arikikapakapa)
description: New Zealand's only geothermal golf course, where steaming lakes and bubbling mud pools are part of the landscape. Located in Rotorua's volcanic heart, the Arikikapakapa course delivers a round unlike any other in the country.

name: Akarana Golf Club
description: A historic Auckland club established in 1930, known for its accessible and welcoming atmosphere. The parkland layout suits golfers of all abilities and sits in a convenient location close to the city centre.

name: Heritage Golf & Country Club
description: A premium parkland course set in the tranquil rural countryside north of Auckland. Mature landscaping and quality conditioning make Heritage a popular choice for golfers seeking a polished round without leaving the Auckland region.

name: Ohope Beach Golf Links
description: A seaside links near Whakatane ranked in the NZ top 40, offering genuine coastal golf with ocean views and firm, fast-running fairways. One of the Bay of Plenty's finest courses and well worth the trip to the sunny eastern coast.

name: Pupuke Golf Club
description: An established North Shore club with pleasant views over the volcanic Lake Pupuke. The flat, well-maintained layout is ideal for walkers and provides a relaxed yet engaging test of golf close to central Auckland.

name: Takapuna Golf Club
description: A well-established North Shore club with views across the Hauraki Gulf to iconic Rangitoto Island. The mature parkland course is a favourite among Auckland golfers for its scenic outlook and convenient location.

name: Mount Maunganui Golf Club
description: A popular links-style course at the foot of iconic Mauao (Mount Maunganui), one of New Zealand's most recognisable landmarks. The coastal setting, reliable Bay of Plenty sunshine, and nearby beach make it a must-play for visiting golfers.

name: Manawatu Golf Club
description: Palmerston North's premier club, offering a top-quality parkland layout with well-conditioned fairways and true greens. The Manawatu Golf Club provides one of the best tests of golf in the lower North Island and has a proud history of competitive play.

name: Otago Golf Club
description: One of Dunedin's established parkland clubs, offering a mature tree-lined layout with well-kept greens. A solid test of golf in a traditional setting within easy reach of the city centre.

name: Whangarei Golf & Country Club
description: The premier club in Northland's largest city, offering a well-maintained parkland layout that suits golfers of all abilities. Mature trees and tidy presentation make this a reliable choice when visiting the Whangarei area.

name: Taupo Golf Club (Centennial)
description: A public parkland course beside Lake Taupo, offering affordable golf with spectacular lake and mountain scenery. The relaxed atmosphere and stunning backdrop make Centennial a must-play for visitors to the central North Island.

name: Hamilton Golf Club
description: A long-established Waikato club set beside the Waikato River in Hamilton. Mature trees, river views, and a well-conditioned parkland layout make it a respected fixture of the regional golfing calendar.

name: Bay of Islands Golf Club
description: A friendly parkland course in the heart of the Bay of Islands, one of New Zealand's most popular holiday destinations. Its relaxed atmosphere and pleasant layout make it a great addition to any Northland golf trip.

name: Whitford Park Golf Club
description: A scenic parkland course in the Whitford rural area east of Auckland. Peaceful surroundings and a well-maintained layout make it a pleasant escape from the city, just a short drive from the motorway.

name: Hagley Golf Club
description: A popular public course in Hagley Park near the Christchurch CBD, offering accessible golf in a beautiful park setting. The flat, walkable layout is ideal for casual rounds, with mature trees framing the fairways.

name: Chisholm Links Golf Club
description: A links-style course perched beside St Clair Beach on the Dunedin coast, where sea breezes add an extra dimension to every round. The ocean views and accessible location make it a popular choice for visitors exploring the city.

name: Judgeford Golf Club
description: A scenic parkland course tucked into the tranquil Judgeford valley between Wellington and the Hutt Valley. The rolling terrain, native bush backdrop, and peaceful setting make for an enjoyable escape from the city.

name: Hawkes Bay Golf Club
description: The main parkland course in the Art Deco city of Napier, with a welcoming visitor policy that makes it easy to get a game. A well-maintained layout in one of Hawke's Bay's sunniest and most vibrant destinations.

name: Windross Farm Golf Course
description: A water-feature-rich parkland course south of Auckland, where lakes and streams come into play on numerous holes. The thoughtful design and attractive landscaping provide an enjoyable challenge for golfers of all levels.

name: Tauranga Golf Club
description: A well-established club with a quality parkland layout in the heart of Tauranga. Mature trees and well-maintained greens provide a satisfying test of golf in one of New Zealand's fastest-growing and sunniest cities.

name: St Andrews Golf Club Hamilton
description: A quality parkland course in Hamilton with good visitor access and well-maintained facilities. Its accessible layout and welcoming atmosphere make it a solid choice for golfers passing through the Waikato.

name: Hutt Golf Club
description: An established Hutt Valley club with a traditional parkland layout featuring mature trees and well-kept greens. The course offers a reliable, pleasant round in a convenient location for Wellington-area golfers.

name: Invercargill Golf Club
description: The premier club in Southland, consistently ranked among the top 60 courses in New Zealand. Set among mature trees in the Otatara suburb of Invercargill, it offers a well-conditioned parkland test that rewards accurate shot-making.

name: Nelson Golf Club
description: A scenic parkland course in Nelson, New Zealand's sunniest city, with a beautiful mountain backdrop framing the fairways. The generous sunshine and well-maintained layout make it one of the most reliably playable courses in the country throughout the year.

name: Rotorua Golf Club (Springfield)
description: A second Rotorua option set through the forest park, offering a different character to the city's main course. Native bush and towering trees line the fairways, creating a peaceful, nature-filled round.

name: New Plymouth Golf Club
description: The main club in New Plymouth, where the spectacular backdrop of snow-capped Mt Taranaki dominates the skyline from nearly every hole. The well-established parkland course offers quality golf in one of the North Island's most scenic volcanic settings.

name: Miramar Golf Club
description: Conveniently located near Wellington Airport, this course offers harbour views and a compact layout that suits golfers short on time. The elevated positions on several holes provide panoramic vistas across Evans Bay and the surrounding hills.

name: Mangawhai Golf Club
description: A popular, visitor-friendly course near the surf and sand of Mangawhai Heads. The well-kept layout offers an enjoyable round in a laid-back coastal setting just 90 minutes north of Auckland.

name: Omaha Golf Club
description: A coastal community course near the popular Omaha Beach holiday area, about an hour north of Auckland. The relaxed seaside atmosphere and tidy layout make it a natural fit for a holiday round.

name: Norsewood Golf Club
description: A quaint 9-hole country course in the Scandinavian-heritage town of Norsewood, offering a fun and challenging layout for golfers of all levels. The course measures 5,281 metres over 18 holes and is open year-round, providing an authentic rural New Zealand golfing experience in the Tararua District.

name: Maraenui Golf Club
description: A challenging course in Napier with over 800 members and modern facilities.

name: Puketitiri Golf Club
description: A rural 9-hole in the Puketitiri valley inland from Napier.

name: Te Pohue Golf Club
description: A small backcountry 9-hole on SH5 between Napier and Taupo.

name: Castlepoint Golf Club
description: A charming 9-hole coastal course near the popular Castlepoint Beach and lighthouse on the Wairarapa coast. Established in 1969 and maintained by dedicated local volunteers, this good-value country course is especially popular with holidaymakers during summer.

name: Ngawi Hitaround Golf Club
description: The southernmost course on the North Island, this quirky 9-hole layout sits right on the beachfront approaching the tiny settlement of Ngawi on the Cape Palliser Road. Square greens mown into seaside grass and holes named after maritime misadventures give this rugged coastal course a character all its own.

name: Ohariu Valley Golf Club
description: A friendly 9-hole course set in a quiet, scenic country valley northwest of Wellington, where the soundtrack is birdsong and the occasional sheep. The peaceful rural setting provides a genuine escape from city life, with virtually no traffic and only one hole running alongside the road.

name: Otaki Golf Club
description: Renowned as the best course on the Kapiti Coast, Otaki sits in a beautiful rural environment just a minute from Otaki township. Less than an hour's drive from both Wellington and Palmerston North, the well-maintained layout offers a quality round in a tranquil country setting.

name: RNZAF Wellington Golf Club
description: A tidy 18-hole course on the grounds of the Royal New Zealand Air Force base in Upper Hutt. Open to the public, this par-71 layout offers good value and a well-maintained parkland setting in the upper Hutt Valley.

name: The Morgans - Pauatahanui Golf Course
description: A relaxed 9-hole golf retreat nestled on Paekakariki Hill Road in Pauatahanui, reached via a tranquil one-kilometre drive through native bush. Restored by the Morgan family in 2019, the course welcomes all players in a stress-free, non-membership environment surrounded by a nature reserve.

name: Wainuiomata Golf Club
description: Relaxed golf in a wonderful natural setting just 25 minutes from Wellington CBD, where tui, lorikeet, and kereru frequent the bush-clad hills of the surrounding countryside. The course offers a peaceful escape with native birdsong providing the soundtrack to your round.

name: Hutt Park Golf Club
description: A compact 9-hole course in Moera, Lower Hutt.

name: Mahunga Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course in Masterton on the Wairarapa plains.

name: Mornington Golf Club
description: Established in 1916 on the Berhampore Golf Course in Wellington. Strong inter-club structure with a first-class layout.

name: Shandon Golf Club
description: Founded in 1927 on Gear Island in Petone, providing an excellent test for all golfers. Has hosted several national tournaments.

name: Fitzroy Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course in the Fitzroy suburb of New Plymouth.

name: Manukorihi Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course at Tikorangi in the Taranaki countryside.

name: Westown Golf Club
description: One of Taranaki's leading courses, situated 8 km from central New Plymouth on Mangorei Road off SH3.

name: Eltham Golf Club
description: Built in 1902, this underrated 12-hole course in the Taranaki town of Eltham features natural water hazards, strategic bunkers, and a signature amphitheatre green on the 12th hole. Dual tees allow the course to play as a full 18, offering excellent variety and value.

name: Manaia Golf Club
description: Founded in 1905, this flat 18-hole course in south Taranaki is set amid prime dairy farmland with views of Mt Taranaki and greens generally rated the best in the district. The course features a historic Maori Pa and the Manaia Redoubt within its boundaries, with a walkway along the banks of the Waiokura Stream adding to its unique character.

name: Pungarehu Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course along scenic State Highway 45 in Taranaki, offering views of Mt Egmont, the Tasman Sea, and the Cape Egmont Lighthouse. The layout winds around a historic Pa site and volcanic lahars, creating a unique golfing landscape with genuine character.

name: Strathmore Golf Club
description: A rugged 9-hole country course in rural eastern Taranaki with 14 tees for variety over 18 holes. The most easterly course in the region, Strathmore offers views of Mt Taranaki and an authentic back-country golfing experience.

name: Urenui Golf Club
description: A coastal 9-hole course with alternative greens and tees for an 18-hole game, located 20 minutes north of New Plymouth with some holes backing onto Urenui Beach. Tempting doglegs and pohutukawa-lined fairways create a short but enjoyable layout, popular with holidaymakers drawn to the neighbouring beach and campground.

name: Apiti Golf Club
description: A flat 9-hole course set against the stunning backdrop of the Ruahine Ranges in the Oroua Valley, about 4 km north of Apiti township in northern Manawatu. One of the most affordable clubs in New Zealand, it closes briefly in September for lambing season, adding to its authentic rural character.

name: Castlecliff Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course in Whanganui midway between Wellington and New Plymouth on the west coast, boasting views of Mounts Taranaki and Ruapehu as well as stunning vistas across the Tasman Sea to the South Island. The expansive panoramas make this one of the most scenic courses in the lower North Island.

name: Hawkestone Golf Club
description: A welcoming 9-hole course on the banks of the Kakariki lakes near Halcombe, with 18 tee blocks and dual pin placements providing variety over a full round. Founded in 1930, the course offers views across the Manawatu and Rangitikei regions in a relaxed country setting.

name: Pahiatua Golf Club
description: Known as "The Jewel of the Bush," Pahiatua Golf Club sits on the banks of the Mangatainoka River between Pahiatua and Woodville, near the iconic Tui Brewery on State Highway 2. The riverside setting and lush surrounding bush create a distinctive and memorable golfing experience.

name: Rangitikei Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course near Bulls, endorsed by Craig Perks, 2002 Players Championship winner.

name: Tawhero Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course in the Gonville suburb of Whanganui.

name: Totaradale Golf Club
description: A tranquil 9-hole course on the outskirts of Wakefield village, a 15-minute drive south of Richmond.

name: Awatere Golf Club
description: Established in 1927, this friendly 9-hole club sits on the southern side of the Awatere River near Seddon in Marlborough. The course is open seven days a year and welcomes visitors to enjoy a relaxed round in a picturesque wine country setting.

name: Koura Bay Golf Course
description: A beautifully maintained 9-hole resort course set on a plateau at the foot of the ranges overlooking the North Kaikoura coast and peninsula. The course offers two tee-offs per hole for an 18-hole rating, with panoramic ocean views and a relaxed atmosphere.

name: Murchison Golf Club
description: A hidden gem near the Buller River, just 2 km north of Murchison in the Tasman region. This flat, relaxed 9-hole course offers a picturesque setting surrounded by native bush and mountain views.

name: Rarangi Golf Club
description: Nestled between the surf of Cloudy Bay and bush-clad hills dominated by Mount Robertson, Rarangi offers a unique all-seasons experience. Golfers can enjoy the rhythm of the surf, watch tui and fantails, and take in the bush-covered backdrop while playing a course that challenges all skill levels.

name: Redstone Golf Park
description: A charming 9-hole country course set in tranquil gardens, 30 minutes from Nelson near Wakefield. The flat layout features numerous water hazards and is welcoming to beginners, while experienced golfers will appreciate the challenge. An on-site cafe and disc golf course add to the relaxed atmosphere.

name: Wairau Valley Golf Club
description: A beautifully kept and picturesque rural 9-hole in the heart of the Marlborough region, 40 km southwest of Blenheim on SH 63. The course offers wonderful views of the nearby Richmond Range and features the infamous "Shady Lane" par 4.

name: Ben Ohau Golf Club
description: A scenic 9-hole course with 16 tees in the heart of the Mackenzie Country near Twizel, offering magnificent views of Aoraki/Mount Cook and the surrounding peaks. The high-country setting and crisp mountain air make every round here truly special.

name: Cheviot Golf Club
description: A rare 12-hole layout established in 1925, set five minutes west of Cheviot township in North Canterbury. The course features views of the Kaikoura Mountains and a tranquil stream weaving through the fairways, offering an ideal length when 18 is too much and 9 too few.

name: Everglades Country Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course established in 1967, located 20 minutes north of central Christchurch. Bordered by the Kaputone stream on two sides, the challenge lies in navigating tree-lined fairways and relatively compact greens.

name: Greendale Golf Club
description: Situated 40 km from Christchurch on the banks of the Selwyn River, this course offers 18 holes of relaxed country golf. Well maintained by a full-time greenkeeper, with irrigated greens, tee blocks, and partial fairway watering ensuring excellent playing conditions.

name: Hawarden Golf Club
description: A well-manicured 9-hole in the Hurunui region of North Canterbury, established in 1924 and set beside the village of Hawarden. The course sits on two levels separated by a stream, with tree-lined fairways and exceptional attention paid to the greens.

name: Kaituna Golf Club
description: A unique 9-hole course on Kaitorete Spit, 48 km south of Christchurch off the main Akaroa highway. The tussock-covered, free-draining terrain means the course stays playable year-round, even when other Canterbury courses are waterlogged in winter.

name: Mackenzie Golf Club
description: A rural 9-hole in the Mackenzie Country with views toward the Southern Alps and surrounding high-country farmland. The peaceful setting and uncrowded fairways make it an appealing stop for golfers exploring the region.

name: Maungati Golf Club
description: A character-filled 9-hole course in a valley between the extinct volcano Mt Horrible and the Hunter Hills, north of Waimate. The unique layout and dramatic landscape offer a classic South Canterbury country golfing experience.

name: Mt Nessing Golf Club
description: Established in 1939 near Albury in the Mackenzie Country, this 9-hole course features several memorable holes. The signature first hole, "Aorangi," rewards golfers on clear days with a perfect view of Aoraki/Mount Cook northward over Burkes Pass.

name: Scargill Golf Club
description: Established in 1934 in the Scargill Valley, just one hour north of Christchurch off State Highway 1. This welcoming rural 9-hole is set among rolling North Canterbury hills and open countryside, offering a relaxed yet rewarding experience.

name: Temuka Golf Club
description: Located 1 km east of State Highway 1 on parkland within the Temuka town boundary. The accessible, flat layout makes it an easy and enjoyable course for golfers of all levels visiting South Canterbury.

name: Terrace Downs High Country Resort & Golf Club
description: New Zealand's only high-country golf course, set just one hour from Christchurch near Mt Hutt ski field and Methven. This par 72 championship layout delivers breathtaking views from every hole, with the Southern Alps providing a dramatic alpine backdrop.

name: Waimate Golf Club
description: A beautifully maintained course on the western outskirts of Waimate, 47 km south of Timaru. The signature 18th is a deceptively challenging 410-metre par 4, capping off an enjoyable round through well-kept Canterbury countryside.

name: Weedons Country Club
description: A quality 18-hole par 73 course just 20 minutes south of Christchurch Square, featuring tree-lined fairways and numerous doglegs that challenge the best golfers. The country club atmosphere and well-maintained layout make it a popular choice in the Selwyn district.

name: Avondale Golf Club
description: A testing 18-hole course on the east side of Christchurch, approximately 10 minutes from the city centre towards New Brighton.

name: Bottle Lake Golf Club
description: A welcoming club in the Parklands area of Christchurch, formerly known as Burwood then Windsor. More than 50 years of history.

name: Coringa Golf Club
description: One of Christchurch's premier golfing destinations on McLeans Island Road, offering a picturesque and challenging 18-hole championship course.

name: Harewood Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course in the Harewood area of Christchurch, close to the airport.

name: Rawhiti Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course in New Brighton, Christchurch.

name: Waimairi Beach Golf Club
description: A professional and friendly club in the Parklands area of Christchurch with a strong reputation for welcoming players of all abilities.

name: Waitikiri Golf Club
description: Located in the north-east of Christchurch opposite Bottle Lake Forest, only 15 minutes from the city centre. Recognised as one of the top courses in Canterbury.

name: Gleniti Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course on the eastern outskirts of Timaru with wonderful views from the Southern Alps to the sea. Founded in 1928.

name: Grande Vue Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course in Geraldine, South Canterbury.

name: Highfield Golf Club
description: Timaru's most conveniently located course, in the heart of the city. A 13-hole layout playable as 9 or 18 from different tees.

name: The Cairns Golf Course
description: A 9-hole course near Lake Tekapo in the Mackenzie Country.

name: Tinwald Golf Club
description: An 18-hole par 72 course on the south side of Ashburton. Country hospitality with a friendly atmosphere welcoming visitors.

name: Allan Grange Golf Club
description: A pleasant 9-hole country course near Balclutha in South Otago, set along the Clutha River. The rolling farmland setting and well-kept fairways offer a relaxing round amid the quiet Otago countryside.

name: Gibbston Valley Golf Club
description: Queenstown's newest golf club, featuring a 9-hole par-32 layout designed by former touring professional Greg Turner within the Gibbston Valley Resort. The course includes inventive double greens and is framed by the vineyard-studded hills of the Gibbston wine region.

name: Linton Camp Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course based at Linton Military Camp near Palmerston North. Photo ID is required to enter the camp, but the well-maintained layout and unique military-base setting make the visit worthwhile.

name: Kaitaia Golf Club
description: Known as the 90 Mile Beach Links, this course is situated at Ahipara, just 15 minutes west of Kaitaia. The coastal setting at the southern end of Ninety Mile Beach gives it a character unlike any other course in the Far North.

name: Northern Wairoa Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course perched beside the Tasman Sea at Baylys Beach, just north of Dargaville. Wide fairways, pohutukawa-lined holes, true greens, and notably no bunkers create a distinctive seaside experience with panoramic ocean views.

name: Okaihau Golf Club
description: A scenic 9-hole course with dual tees, established in 1928, sitting halfway between Kerikeri and Kaikohe at an elevation of 200 metres. Near Lake Omapere, the course offers views stretching to the Bay of Islands and a famously warm welcome from local members.

name: Tapora Golf Club
description: Established in 1964 on the undulating sand dunes of the Kaipara Harbour, this 9-hole links course was the first in New Zealand to install synthetic greens. Elevated holes in the middle of the course offer magnificent harbour views, while surrounding farmland and avocado orchards complete the scene.

name: The Pines Golf Club
description: A picturesque course with stunning views of the harbour and Whangarei Heads from many tee, fairway, and green locations. The elevated vantage points and coastal panoramas make this one of the most scenic rounds in the Northland region.

name: Pongaroa Golf Club
description: A welcoming 9-hole course set amidst rural scenery and mature pine trees, located one kilometre west of Pongaroa village. Visitors are always welcome for a relaxing round on this charming country layout in the Tararua District.

name: Waipu Golf Club
description: A lovely parkland course in the Scottish heritage town of Waipu, about an hour north of Auckland. The well-maintained layout and friendly club atmosphere reflect the town's proud community spirit.

name: Helensville Golf Club
description: Established in 1948 and relocated to its current site in 1959, this parkland course is set amid farmland and lifestyle blocks just 35 minutes from downtown Auckland. Tree-lined fairways, American-standard sand-based greens, and tranquil countryside vistas reward the short drive from the city.

name: Manukau Golf Club
description: A well-established South Auckland parkland club with solid facilities and a layout that suits all skill levels. Its accessible location and good value make it a reliable option for golfers in the southern suburbs.

name: Onewhero Golf Club
description: A mature, tree-lined 18-hole course in a rural setting just south of Pukekawa, only 10 minutes from Mercer on SH1. The volcanic, free-draining terrain ensures year-round playability, and challenging water holes add spice to one of the most well-kept courses in the Auckland region.

name: Pukekohe Golf Club
description: Tree-lined fairways, lakes, and a river typify this parkland course that independent critics rate among the best in New Zealand. Superb greens and a layout that challenges golfers of every level make Pukekohe a standout in the South Auckland countryside.

name: RNZAF Auckland Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course within the historic Whenuapai Air Base, established in 1967. Originally serving Royal New Zealand Air Force personnel, it now welcomes a 500-strong membership of military and civilian golfers, with play limited to members and their escorted guests due to the secure base location.

name: Royal NZ Navy Golf Society Golf Club
description: A naval heritage golf society established in 1957 and based on Auckland's North Shore. The society provides an organised competitive and social golfing calendar for members with connections to the Royal New Zealand Navy.

name: South Head Golf Club
description: Located on the picturesque South Kaipara Harbour, about 40 minutes north of Auckland, this course offers an intriguing championship layout with spectacular harbour views. The coastal breezes and water vistas create a memorable setting for a round.

name: Waiuku Golf & Squash Club
description: A challenging coastal course adjoining the township of Waiuku in the southern corner of the Manukau Harbour. Easily accessed from the motorway and offering year-round availability, it provides a breezy, seaside test of golf about 45 minutes south of central Auckland.

name: Porangahau Golf Club
description: Founded in 1927, this free-draining 9-hole links course sits on the stunning east coast of Central Hawke's Bay, offering sea views and alternate tee grounds for variety. Part of the Porangahau Country Club, the course is about 30 minutes from Waipukurau and enjoys a beautiful coastal backdrop near Porangahau Beach.

name: Howick Golf Club
description: An established East Auckland club with scenic coastal views across the Hauraki Gulf. The mature layout and welcoming atmosphere make it a popular choice for golfers on the eastern side of the city.

name: Huapai Golf Club
description: A hidden gem just 20 minutes from the Auckland CBD, offering an affordable and welcoming round. Its convenient location and friendly club culture make it a great option for a casual weekday game.

name: Maungakiekie Golf Club
description: One of Auckland's largest clubs, located in Mt Roskill. A well-presented 18-hole course popular with golfers of all abilities, with good practice facilities and a welcoming atmosphere.

name: Pakuranga Golf Club
description: Conveniently located in the heart of East Auckland between Botany and Howick. A friendly, supportive club with quality golfing and social facilities.

name: Wattle Downs Golf Club
description: A welcoming 9-hole course in Manurewa, South Auckland.

name: Waitakere Golf Club
description: Nestled in the Waitakere Ranges surrounded by native bush and birdsong. Only 30 minutes from the city, but feels a world away.

name: Northridge Golf Resort
description: A picturesque 9-hole course in the Wainui area north of Auckland, set on a scenic lodge property.

name: Horsham Downs Golf Club
description: A welcoming 9-hole course established in 1944 on the banks of the Waikato River, just north of Hamilton city. Known as the friendly club of the Waikato, its picturesque riverside setting and well-maintained layout suit golfers of every level.

name: Hukanui Golf Club
description: Founded in 1935, this challenging 9-hole course features tree-lined fairways, manicured greens, and well-placed bunkers across flat to gently rolling terrain. A solid test for golfers of all levels in the heart of the Waikato.

name: Huntly Golf Club
description: A welcoming 18-hole course on the west bank of the Waikato River, just north of Huntly. Its central location makes it a convenient stop between Auckland, Hamilton, and Tauranga, all within about an hour's drive.

name: Kawhia Golf Club
description: A relaxed 9-hole course on the remote west coast of the Waikato, offering harbour views from several tee boxes. The easy rolling terrain and friendly atmosphere make it a pleasant stop for golfers exploring the Kawhia area.

name: Ngahinepouri Golf Club
description: Established over 90 years ago, this friendly 9-hole country course offers fully watered greens and fairways in an easy walking layout. Just 20 minutes from central Hamilton, it delivers genuine country hospitality and an enjoyable experience for golfers of all levels.

name: Okoroire Golf Club
description: A charming 9-hole course owned by the Okoroire Hot Springs Hotel, set on undulating terrain near Tirau. No tee time bookings are required, making it an easygoing stop for golfers passing through the Waikato.

name: Paeroa Golf Club Inc.
description: Established in 1904, this 18-hole par 72 course is set in the picturesque Rotokohu Valley near Paeroa. The relatively flat layout features a variety of hazards and water features that keep every round interesting, all framed by the natural beauty of the Waikato countryside.

name: Pauanui Sports & Recreation Club Inc.
description: A holiday golf destination in the Coromandel beach town of Pauanui, offering two compact courses. The relaxed coastal setting and accessible layout make it ideal for a casual round between beach and bush.

name: Pirongia Golf Club Inc.
description: An easy-walking 18-hole par 72 course at the foot of Mount Pirongia, bordered by the historic Waipa River. The relaxed country club atmosphere and stunning mountain views make it a rewarding day out, just 30 minutes south of Hamilton.

name: Putaruru Golf Club
description: A beautifully manicured 18-hole par 72 parkland course dating back to 1920, featuring tree-lined fairways and well-maintained greens in the rural Waikato town of Lichfield. Its rich history and welcoming atmosphere make it a rewarding stop for visiting golfers.

name: Tahuna Golf Club
description: An authentic country 18-hole course where sheep share the fairways and fenced greens add rural character. Located 18 kilometres from Morrinsville on the Tahuna Road, it offers a genuine New Zealand country golf experience at very affordable rates.

name: Taumarunui Golf Club
description: The Tarrangower Course, rated among New Zealand's Top 50, was established in the early 1920s in the heart of the King Country. Its undulating all-weather fairways present a different challenge on every hole, with magnificent views from the clubhouse across the surrounding hills. A rewarding detour for golfers travelling between Lake Taupo and Mount Ruapehu.

name: Te Akau Golf Club
description: A challenging 9-hole country course set in an idyllic valley forty minutes west of Ngaruawahia. Elevated tees atop rocky outcrops, rolling fairways, lakes, mature trees, and resident sheep all combine to test your skill in a uniquely rural Waikato setting.

name: Te Kowhai Golf Club
description: A well-established 9-hole course with narrow fairways that challenge both beginners and experienced golfers. Located just 8 kilometres from Hamilton, it offers a social, friendly atmosphere and easy walking between holes.

name: The Dunes Matarangi Golf Club
description: Originally designed by New Zealand golfing legend Sir Bob Charles, this 18-hole course sits on the furthest tip of the Coromandel Peninsula at Matarangi. The back nine weaves through tall pine trees with wonderful views across Whangapoua Harbour and onto the Pacific Ocean. A quartet of par fives on the inward half rewards long hitters.

name: Waihi Golf Club
description: A pleasant course located just south of the historic gold-mining town of Waihi, near the gateway to the Coromandel Peninsula. A convenient option for golfers travelling between the Waikato and the Bay of Plenty.

name: Waiterimu Golf Club
description: A beautifully presented 9-hole course nestled in rural Waikato, maintained by a dedicated team of volunteer members. One of the most affordable clubs in the region, it is playable year-round and offers a genuine country golf experience.

name: Walton Golf Club
description: Set in the lush green Waikato countryside, Walton offers a warm welcome to visitors with an easy-to-reach location roughly midway between Hamilton, Tauranga, and Auckland. A friendly rural club that rewards a relaxed round.

name: Hamurana Park Golf Club
description: A lovely 9-hole course on the north shore of Lake Rotorua, set within the Hamurana Springs Nature Park. Crystal-clear freshwater springs, a towering Redwood grove, and abundant native birdlife make the surroundings as memorable as the golf.

name: Takapau Golf Club
description: Built in 1898, this well-maintained country course in Central Hawke's Bay features interesting holes set around a meandering stream. Multiple tee configurations, including a Red course for young and casual players, ensure golfers of all abilities are well catered for in this historic rural setting.

name: Omanu Golf Club
description: The largest club in the Bay of Plenty, located on Matapihi Road near Mt Maunganui. Heron frequent the course, inspiring the club's logo.

name: Otumoetai Golf Club
description: Situated in the heart of Tauranga City, offering a friendly 9-hole course suitable for all skill levels.

name: Kinloch Village Golf Club
description: A boutique 11-hole course in the heart of Kinloch Village, near the shores of Lake Taupo. Its unique layout and relaxed atmosphere make it a charming alternative to the region's larger courses.

name: Murupara Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course established in 1958 alongside the Rangitaiki River, about 45 minutes south of Rotorua. The rural setting and riverside location provide a peaceful round in the heart of the Bay of Plenty backcountry.

name: Renner Park Golf Club
description: Nine holes of easy walking set among the rolling hills and native trees of Oropi, just minutes from Greerton Village. A peaceful country setting with pleasant rural views across the western Bay of Plenty.

name: Reporoa Golf Club
description: An 18-hole par 71 course in the Waiotapu Valley near Reporoa, featuring flat to rolling terrain on a pumice base. A straightforward, enjoyable layout on the road between Rotorua and Taupo.

name: Springfield Golf Club
description: The course where former world amateur number one Danny Lee developed his game, earning a reputation for rewarding enterprising play. A layout that encourages creative shot-making and strategic thinking in a welcoming Bay of Plenty setting.

name: Te Teko Golf Club
description: An 18-hole countryside course near Te Teko with well-maintained, wide-open fairways and established trees. A relaxed atmosphere ideal for casual golfers and groups looking for an uncrowded round in the Bay of Plenty.

name: Turangi Golf Club
description: An 18-hole par 72 course at the gateway to Tongariro National Park, formed in 1967 and opened in its full layout by 1971. Reasonably flat with water features and good tree coverage, it sits in a stunning volcanic landscape just south of Taupo.

name: Waikite Valley Golf Club
description: A friendly and social 9-hole course established in 1985, featuring hilly terrain and breathtaking views of the lush Waikite Valley countryside. A charming rural layout between Rotorua and Taupo that rewards accuracy and strategic play.

name: Tahunga Golf Club
description: A seasonal 9-hole country course wrapped by the Hangaroa River, located one hour inland from Gisborne between the Rere and Waerengaokuri districts. Golf in its purest rural form, with rough edges, character, and a welcoming community hub.

name: Waikohu Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course set among rolling farmland near Te Karaka, about 30 minutes from Gisborne. An active community club with members who regularly compete at regional and national level, including the NZ Maori Golf Association championships.

name: Hedgehope Golf Club
description: A short, testing 9-hole layout dating back to 1968, featuring deceptively tricky greens surrounded by mature trees. A great example of friendly, rural Southland golf where the welcome is always warm.

name: Otautau Golf Club
description: An undulating 9-hole course near the Western Southland town of Otautau, with several testing holes that keep the round interesting. The rural setting and welcoming club make it a pleasant stop for visitors in the region.

name: Riversdale Golf Club
description: A testing 9-hole course in the Eastern Southland town of Riversdale, where water hazards, trees, and several dogleg holes demand thoughtful course management. The layout is just a short walk from the town centre.

name: Waikaka Golf Club
description: An interesting, undulating 9-hole course 20 minutes north of Gore, featuring ponds, trees, and boundary fences that keep every shot honest. The friendly local membership and modest green fees make it a welcoming stop in Eastern Southland.

name: Northland Golf Club
description: A beautiful course set in the valley between Mt Hurupaki and Mt Parakiori in the Northland region. The twin volcanic backdrops and mature native plantings give this layout a sense of place that is hard to match.

name: Paparoa Golf Club
description: A true rural golfing experience in a lovely valley in the Kaipara District, just 20 minutes off State Highway 1. The 9-hole layout features well-protected greens and is split down the middle by a quiet country road, adding quirky charm to every round.

name: Rawene Golf Club
description: A charming 9-hole course overlooking the Hokianga Harbour in the historic town of Rawene. The layout starts flat before climbing to reveal harbour views, and the summer-only season adds to its remote, unspoiled appeal.

name: Sherwood Park Golf Club
description: Situated just 7 km from Whangarei, this picturesque course is set among beautiful groves of native trees complemented by natural stone walls and native birdlife. The secluded setting provides an ideal atmosphere for a relaxing yet challenging round, and visitors can be sure of a warm welcome.

name: Waiotira Golf Club
description: A welcoming 9-hole course established in 1947 in the scenic Northland countryside near Whangarei. Originally named "Kieowai" Golf Club, its history reflects the union of the Waikiekie and Waiotira districts, and its affordable, community-focused spirit endures today.

name: Wellsford Golf and Squash Club Inc.
description: Less than an hour north of Auckland Harbour Bridge on State Highway 1, this course offers a friendly country atmosphere with a competitive and challenging layout suitable for all ages.

name: Whangaroa Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course on State Highway 10 in the Far North, with mown fairways flanked by mature trees and small, well-kept greens. The course rating sits more than three shots under its par of 70, rewarding accurate play in a peaceful Northland setting.

name: Awhitu Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course on the Awhitu Peninsula, set within the Awhitu Regional Park with excellent views of the Manukau Harbour and surrounding parkland. Two flags on each green and alternative tees on some holes allow for a varied 18-hole experience in a peaceful, uncrowded setting.

name: Clarks Beach Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course on the shores of the Manukau Harbour, praised by professionals for one of the best collections of par 3s in the country. Native pohutukawa trees, feature fountains amid the ponds, and a par-71 layout that punches well above its weight make this a hidden gem only 40 minutes from central Auckland.

name: Maxwells Golf Club
description: A convenient 9-hole course just 30 minutes south of Auckland city, perfect for a casual round. Indoor training facilities include a golf simulator offering famous courses like Augusta and Pebble Beach.

name: North Shore Golf Club
description: A 27-hole facility on the upper fringes of the Waitemata Harbour near Albany, offering three distinct 18-hole combinations. Tree-lined holes traverse undulating terrain above the Lucas Creek escarpment, delivering scenic rural views just 10 minutes north of the Harbour Bridge.

name: Redwood Park Golf Club
description: A beautifully scenic 18-hole course nestled below the Waitakere Ranges at Swanson, only 15 km from Auckland city. Established in 1970, Redwood Park is known for its friendly and social atmosphere amid a lush native bush setting.

name: The Green Pinnacle
description: Auckland's first luxury indoor golf venue, housed in the beautifully restored Grey Lynn Cameo Cinema. Eleven TrackMan-powered simulator bays deliver hyper-realistic gameplay across 300 virtual courses, making it New Zealand's only affiliated indoor golf club.

name: Waiheke Island Golf Club
description: Voted the best 9-hole course in the northern region, Waiheke Island's course has expanded from its original 1973 layout to 11 holes played from 18 tee blocks. Mature trees and picturesque water views make it a wonderful excuse to catch the ferry from downtown Auckland.

name: Waitemata Golf Club
description: Founded in 1905 in the historic seaside village of Devonport, this course is nestled between Mt Victoria and Narrow Neck Beach. The former Takapuna Jockey Club site still shows the contours of the old "Back Straight" on the par-5 13th, blending rich local history with harbour-side golf just a ferry ride from central Auckland.

name: Warkworth Golf Club
description: Auckland's premier country golf club since 1908, set in the heart of the Matakana wine region just 40 minutes north of the Harbour Bridge. The heritage and surroundings make it an ideal pairing with a vineyard visit.

name: Whangaparaoa Golf Club
description: Established in 1954 near the end of the Whangaparaoa Peninsula, this 18-hole club caters to golfers of all ages and abilities. The peninsular setting offers coastal breezes and pleasant sea views, about 45 minutes from the Harbour Bridge.

name: Coromandel Golf Club
description: Rated among the top 10 nine-hole courses in New Zealand, this picturesque layout sits on the outskirts of Coromandel Town across two adjoining valleys. About two and a half hours from Auckland, it rewards the journey with a challenging and scenic round on the Coromandel Peninsula.

name: Hauraki Golf Club
description: Nestled between rolling hills and the Hauraki Plains, this 18-hole country course is an easy drive from Auckland, Hamilton, and Tauranga. Ideally situated as a "meet in the middle" venue, it offers a peaceful escape from the bustle of bigger city courses.

name: Lakes Resort Pauanui
description: A premier 18-hole championship course designed by Sid Puddicombe, set in a picturesque valley of native wetlands and serene lakes on the Coromandel Peninsula. Notable features include a boardwalk between holes lined with Maori carvings and excellent bunkering throughout. Recognised as one of New Zealand's top courses, it has hosted events including the Nagle Charles Challenge Trophy.

name: Mangakino Golf Club
description: A flat, undulating 9-hole course established in 1951, offering picturesque views of Lake Maraetai and the surrounding forests. Although classed as 9 holes, separate 9th and 18th greens create a full 18-hole experience with different angles on each loop.

name: Morrinsville Golf Club
description: A varied 18-hole course featuring mature trees, gullies, lakes, and well-placed bunkers. Located on the town boundary of Morrinsville, it offers an immensely enjoyable round with easy access to local shops and amenities.

name: Ngaruawahia Golf Club
description: Situated on the banks of the Waikato River just 10 minutes north of Hamilton, this well-regarded course is one of the largest clubs in the Waikato region. Its strong competitive programme and convenient location make it a popular choice for visitors and members alike.

name: Piopio Aria Golf Club
description: A hidden gem in the King Country, this 18-hole par 70 course winds through attractive farmland where friendly sheep graze the fairways. The rolling terrain and honesty-box system capture the spirit of authentic rural New Zealand golf.

name: Purangi Golf & Country Club Inc.
description: A friendly 9-hole course nestled among the Coromandel Peninsula resort towns of Hot Water Beach, Hahei, and Cooks Beach. Popular with holidaymakers, it offers a relaxed round in a stunning coastal setting.

name: Riverside Golf Club
description: Formed in 2013 from the merger of Narrows Golf Club and Lochiel Golf Club, Riverside offers a unique 36-hole option with courses on both sides of the Waikato River. Two distinct layouts within a 5-kilometre drive give members and visitors excellent variety.

name: Stewart Alexander Golf Club
description: Set in the peaceful rural surrounds of Te Awamutu, this course offers a relaxed golfing experience free from traffic noise. Just 30 minutes from Hamilton and two hours from Auckland, it combines beautiful countryside scenery with a warm, welcoming club culture.

name: Tairua Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course on the northern side of the charming Coromandel township of Tairua. The club welcomes visitors on club days and provides a pleasant round in a relaxed coastal setting.

name: Te Aroha Golf Club
description: Set on the beautiful foothills of the Kaimai Ranges beneath Mount Te Aroha, this course offers a variety of flat and sloping holes that appeal to all levels. Surrounded by farmland and just minutes from the town centre, it combines scenic mountain views with accessible golf.

name: Tirau Golf Club
description: An immaculate parkland course situated between State Highways 1 and 27 in the heart of the Waikato. Its central location makes it a short drive from Rotorua, Waitomo Caves, Taupo, Hamilton, and Tauranga, perfect for a round while exploring the region.

name: Waikare Golf Club
description: A welcoming course in the village of Te Kauwhata, conveniently located less than an hour from both Auckland and Hamilton and just 2 kilometres from State Highway 1. Its accessible position makes it an easy stop for golfers on the move.

name: Waitomo Golf & Country Club
description: Located in the heart of the Waikato near the famous Waitomo Caves, this course provides a pleasant round in attractive countryside. Just 5 minutes south of Otorohanga on State Highway 3, it is a natural complement to a day of cave exploration.

name: Fairview Golf Club
description: Established in 1998 and designed to championship standard, this course is located in Katikati between Waihi and Tauranga. A well-regarded layout that offers a serious test of golf in the western Bay of Plenty.

name: Hinehopu Golf Club
description: A delightfully picturesque course on the eastern shore of Lake Rotoiti, surrounded by native bush. Well-groomed fairways and compact greens demand accuracy on every shot, rewarding precise iron play in a serene lakeside setting.

name: Lake Rotoiti Golf Course
description: A unique 10-hole layout built in 1997, beginning with a deceptively short opener featuring an island-style green surrounded by water. Set alongside Lake Rotoiti, the course offers a balanced and scenic test for golfers of all abilities.

name: Lake View Golf and Country Club Golf Club
description: A popular 18-hole course set amongst cleverly positioned native and exotic trees on delightfully undulating terrain, just a short drive from Rotorua. The peace, tranquility, and extraordinary native birdlife make it a hidden treasure of the Bay of Plenty.

name: Omokoroa Golf Club
description: A stunning harbourside 18-hole course on the Omokoroa Peninsula, blending the best of links and parkland design. Easy walking and picturesque views across the Tauranga Harbour make it one of the region's most scenic rounds, just 15 minutes north of the city.

name: Summerhill Golf Course
description: Perched on top of the Papamoa Hills, this course offers captivating sea views and picturesque parkland surrounds. The elevated position provides panoramic vistas across the Bay of Plenty coastline, creating a relaxed and memorable golfing experience.

name: Patutahi Golf Club
description: A small country club 20 minutes from Gisborne city, renowned for its top-quality greens. The well-maintained putting surfaces and peaceful rural surroundings make it a rewarding detour from the main Gisborne courses.

name: Te Puia Hot Springs Golf Club
description: An 18-hole hilltop course on the East Cape overlooking the Pacific Ocean and Mount Hikurangi, featuring raised tees, deep gullies, and forested fairway edges. The annual East Coast Open tournament has drawn golfers from across New Zealand for over 50 years. A truly unique setting that rewards the journey along State Highway 35.

name: Cape Turnagain Golf Club
description: A rugged 9-hole coastal course perched near Cape Turnagain in Hawke's Bay, where the biggest challenge is the ever-present wind. Located about an hour's drive from Dannevirke, this remote course rewards adventurous golfers with a wild, windswept setting along the eastern coastline.

name: Karamu Golf Club
description: A friendly public course situated on State Highway 2, just north of Hastings, taking its name from the Karamu Stream that meanders around the layout. Founded in 2011, the club is conveniently located between Napier, Hastings, and Havelock North, offering a relaxed atmosphere with a driving range and mini golf on site.

name: Onga Onga Golf Club
description: A picturesque 9-hole course nestled in the peaceful surroundings of the Forest Gate domain along Highway 50 in Central Hawke's Bay. Dual tees on front and back nines ensure variety across a full 18-hole round, with well-groomed fairways and a relaxed country atmosphere.

name: Waipawa Golf Club
description: A friendly 12-hole country course in Central Hawke's Bay where booking a tee time is seldom necessary. The relaxed, welcoming atmosphere and easy-going pace make it an ideal stop for golfers exploring the region.

name: Napier Golf Club (Waikouaiti)
description: A traditional Napier club featuring a well-kept parkland layout with mature trees and gentle contours. The course provides a solid test of golf in the sunny Hawke's Bay region, with a welcoming atmosphere for visitors and members alike.

name: Eketahuna Golf Club
description: An 18-hole country course on the edge of Eketahuna, where golfers share the fairways with grazing sheep. Celebrating over a century of golf since 1910, the Makakahi Course offers a unique rural New Zealand experience with a relaxed, turn-up-and-play atmosphere.

name: Karori Golf Club
description: Situated in the scenic South Makara Valley just 13 km from downtown Wellington, this course features 18 diverse holes shaped by natural topography, a meandering stream, and elevated greens rewarded by elevated tees. The layout relies on the land's natural contours rather than man-made mounds and bunkers, creating an authentic and varied golfing experience.

name: Manor Park Golf Sanctuary
description: Established in 1913, Manor Park is an 18-hole championship course and internationally recognised Audubon-certified wildlife sanctuary. Set among beautiful native bush and wetlands with gently rolling fairways bordered by the Hutt River, the course is home to over 20 species of bird. Past members include 2005 US Open champion Michael Campbell and professional Gareth Paddison.

name: Riversdale Beach Golf Club
description: Often described as one of the best little courses in New Zealand, this well-maintained 9-hole course sits on the Wairarapa coastline, about 45 minutes from Masterton. Played twice from different tees to make 18, the layout features views of the sea from both the course and the clubhouse.

name: Te Marua Golf Club
description: An 18-hole A-grade course built on gently undulating ground adjacent to the Hutt River, offering a picturesque round with a rural atmosphere. Located just 10 minutes north of Upper Hutt city centre, the course combines accessibility with a peaceful countryside feel.

name: Titahi Golf Club
description: Home club of 2005 US Open champion Michael Campbell and professional Lynnette Brooky, Titahi has a strong tradition of nurturing champions. The course offers a welcoming atmosphere and solid test of golf on the Porirua coastline north of Wellington.

name: Trentham Camp Golf Club
description: A welcoming 18-hole course based at Trentham Military Camp in Upper Hutt, where the inclusive community atmosphere is the club's hallmark. Members of all ages and abilities play together on club days, making it one of the most social golfing experiences in the Wellington region.

name: Kaitake Golf Club
description: A particularly welcoming and friendly course on the coast just south of New Plymouth, close to the premier beach resort of Oakura. The seaside setting and year-round patronage reflect the pleasant Taranaki climate and relaxed coastal lifestyle along Surf Highway 45.

name: Burnham Golf Club Inc.
description: An 18-hole course nestled in the countryside south of Rolleston, established in 1953. The flat, easy-walking layout features tightly tree-lined fairways that demand accuracy off the tee and precise iron play into the greens.

name: Patea Golf Club
description: A hidden gem perched on the cliffs of the South Taranaki coast, this bunkerless 18-hole links course overlooks the Tasman Sea with views to Mt Taranaki and Mt Ruapehu on clear days. Sheep-grazed fairways and well-maintained greens give the course an authentic, old-school links feel.

name: Te Ngutu Golf Club
description: Known locally as "the best kept secret in golf" and "the jewel of the west," Te Ngutu was founded in 1932 by a group of forward-thinking local residents. The course has maintained its intimate, community spirit while offering a quality round in the rural heartland of South Taranaki.

name: Buckley Golf Club
description: Situated on the foothills of the Tararua Ranges in Shannon, this course has been operating for over 75 years. Located 30 minutes from Palmerston North or an hour north of Wellington, Buckley offers a compact country course in a picturesque hill-country setting.

name: Broadwood Golf Club
description: A compact 9-hole course tucked into the rolling countryside of the Far North. Set amid beautiful Northland farmland, Broadwood offers a quiet, unhurried round well off the beaten track.

name: Orlando Country Club
description: Located on the outskirts of Palmerston North, Orlando Country Club is renowned for hosting corporate events and features a 9-hole course alongside a driving range. The resort-style setting provides a relaxed environment for both social and competitive golf.

name: Rangatira Golf Club
description: A truly unique 18-hole course in the heart of the Rangitikei, built on three levels with stunning views of the Rangitikei River. The highlight is the electric cable car connecting the levels, the only one of its kind on a New Zealand golf course.

name: Golden Downs Golf Club
description: Built in 1946, this parkland 9-hole near Wakefield boasts well-grassed fairways, excellent greens, and a serene bush setting that leaves visitors in awe. It is home to one of the longest par 5s in New Zealand at 659 metres from the black tees.

name: Charteris Bay Golf Club
description: A charming 9-hole on the south side of Lyttelton Harbour, set within the beautiful Orton Bradley Estate. The course offers magnificent views of the harbour, Mt Bradley, and Mt Herbert, combining scenic coastal golf with a peaceful country atmosphere.

name: Marlborough Golf Club
description: Established in 1900 and situated among the vines, this is widely regarded as the finest golf course at the top of the South Island. Its long heritage and Marlborough wine country setting make it a must-play for visitors to the region.

name: Nopera Bay Golf Club
description: The only golf course in the Marlborough Sounds, set on a working farm in the Kenepuru Sound with staggering water and bush views. This remote 9-hole layout features challenging "risk and reward" holes with undulating terrain, sloping greens, and a deep creek running through the course.

name: Onekaka Links Golf Club
description: An extraordinary golfing experience in Golden Bay with stunning ocean vistas and memorable hospitality. The Links Course features one par 5, eight par 4s, and nine par 3s, incorporating double and triple greens, major elevation changes, cliffs, and penal bunkering. The Mountain Course adds a significantly tougher challenge for the adventurous golfer.

name: Tasman Golf Club
description: A spectacular course in Tasman village on the Kina Peninsula, off Highway 60 between Nelson and Motueka. The coastal setting provides beautiful views across Tasman Bay and the surrounding ranges.

name: Whataroa Golf Club
description: A picturesque 9-hole nestled in native bush on the West Coast, with a large creek winding through the course. Located near Franz Josef Glacier, it combines a unique golfing experience with the stunning scenery of South Westland.

name: Akaroa Golf Club
description: Situated at Duvauchelle on Banks Peninsula, just 10 minutes from Akaroa and 90 minutes from Christchurch. Regarded as one of the most scenic courses in Canterbury, the dramatic volcanic harbour landscape provides a breathtaking backdrop to every hole.

name: Amuri Golf Club
description: Established in 1924, this North Canterbury course sits between Rotherham and Waiau among spectacular mountain scenery. Mount Lyford rises to the north while a mountain range frames the western horizon, creating a memorable alpine setting for a round of golf.

name: Culverden Golf Club
description: Established in 1941, this 9-hole course sits on the beautiful Amuri Basin countryside, 37 km south of Hanmer Springs. Views stretch from the inland and seaward Kaikoura Ranges to the Southern Alps, while a winding creek adds challenge to the layout.

name: Ellesmere Golf Club
description: An 18-hole par 72 course located 3 km south of Leeston township. An extensive irrigation system keeps the fairways and greens in excellent condition for year-round golf across the Canterbury Plains.

name: Hanmer Springs Golf Club
description: Set in the charming alpine village of Hanmer Springs, 135 km northwest of Christchurch. The mountain scenery and crisp high-country air create a delightful setting, making this a perfect round to complement a visit to the famous thermal pools.

name: Hororata Golf Club
description: Among the most picturesque clubs in Canterbury, set on two levels of river flats with streams winding through the course. Located in the small rural town of Glentunnel, just 35 minutes west of Christchurch, the natural water features and lush setting create a beautiful golfing environment.

name: Mayfield Golf Club
description: One of the best 9-hole country courses in the Ashburton area, situated on the north bank of the Hinds River. Good drainage keeps the course playable in winter, while fairway irrigation ensures lush conditions through summer.

name: McLeans Island Golf Club
description: Set in the tranquil surroundings of McLeans Island, a short drive from Christchurch city. This small, friendly club welcomes visitors to enjoy a peaceful round in a natural setting away from the urban bustle.

name: Pegasus Golf Club
description: Located just north of Christchurch in the heart of Pegasus town, this course is renowned as one of the best in New Zealand. Set against a diverse landscape of mountains, water features, and the natural wetlands of Pegasus Bay, it delivers a first-class golfing experience.

name: Tai Tapu Golf Club
description: Widely considered the best 9-hole course in Canterbury, Tai Tapu is a pleasant, compact layout just 16 km from Christchurch along the Akaroa Highway. The country setting and quality conditions make it a favourite for golfers seeking a quick but satisfying round.

name: Waimakariri Gorge Golf Club
description: Formed in 1961 on crown land near the Waimakariri Gorge bridge, at the foothills of the magnificent Southern Alps. The course is only 30 minutes from Christchurch International Airport, offering a scenic escape with mountain views in every direction.

name: Barley Station Golf Course
description: A private course on the Crown Terrace near Queenstown, designed by former touring professional Greg Turner. Originally built on a farm owned by America's Cup legend Sir Russell Coutts, the layout takes advantage of the dramatic Central Otago landscape.

name: Clinton Golf Club
description: A friendly 9-hole course in the South Otago township of Clinton, established in 1937. Rolling hills and farmland surround the layout, providing a peaceful setting for a casual round.

name: Frankton Golf Centre
description: A gentle 9-hole course nestled beneath the dramatic backdrop of the Remarkables, ideally suited for beginners and families. Its convenient location next to Queenstown Airport and the Events Centre makes it an easy stop between flights.

name: Gladfield Country Golf Club
description: A relaxed 9-hole country course near Mosgiel on the Taieri Plain, just 15 minutes from Dunedin. Rolling countryside and well-groomed greens make it a pleasant spot for golfers of all abilities.

name: Glenorchy Golf Club
description: A unique 9-hole course in the tiny lakeside village of Glenorchy at the head of Lake Wakatipu. Surrounded by towering mountains and beech forest, it offers one of the most dramatic natural settings of any golf course in New Zealand.

name: Island Park Golf Club
description: A 9-hole parkland course in the Dunedin suburb of Waldronville, enjoying its own sheltered microclimate just 15 minutes from the CBD. The compact layout offers a genuine golfing challenge in a relaxed, family-friendly environment.

name: Kurow Golf Club
description: A pleasant 9-hole course in the heart of the beautiful Waitaki Valley, surrounded by the tussock-covered hills and big skies of the North Otago high country. A friendly stop for golfers travelling between Christchurch and Queenstown.

name: Lawrence Golf Club
description: Established in 1894, this is one of the oldest golf clubs in New Zealand. The flat, easy-walking 9-hole layout near the historic gold-rush town of Lawrence features ornamental trees and elevated tees with views across the Tuapeka countryside.

name: Middlemarch Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course on the edge of the Middlemarch township in the Strath Taieri Valley. The layout stretches over 5,650 metres and provides an enjoyable challenge for visitors exploring the Otago Central Rail Trail region.

name: Omakau Golf Club
description: A delightful 9-hole country course right in the centre of the South Island, bordered by the Otago Central Rail Trail. Every hole reveals new views of the surrounding schist-rock landscape that is so distinctive to Central Otago.

name: Otakou Golf Club
description: A 9-hole links-style course on the Otago Peninsula with a layout of humps, hollows, and contoured greens overlooking the harbour. The honesty-box format and exposed coastal setting give it an authentic, old-school New Zealand golf feel.

name: Otematata Golf Club
description: A compact 9-hole course in the lakeside village of Otematata, conveniently located in the centre of town. It offers a casual round amid the expansive scenery of the upper Waitaki Basin.

name: Port Chalmers Golf Club
description: A scenic 9-hole course blessed with sweeping views across the Otago Harbour. The club is renowned for its friendly, welcoming atmosphere and provides an enjoyable challenge for seasoned players and newcomers alike.

name: Toko Golf Club
description: A pleasant rolling 9-hole course in the South Otago town of Milton, about 40 minutes south of Dunedin. The layout is open to visitors and provides a genuine country-club atmosphere.

name: Waikouaiti Golf Club
description: A welcoming 9-hole country course near the beach, with panoramic views of a lagoon teeming with birdlife. Different tee blocks for the front and back nines give each loop a distinct character.

name: Dipton Golf Club
description: A hilly 9-hole course established in 1952, offering panoramic views of the Oreti Plains from its elevated tees. One of the more testing short layouts in Southland, it rewards a reasonable level of fitness and straight driving.

name: Drummond Golf Club
description: A well-groomed flat 9-hole on the Southland plain between Winton and Invercargill, established in 1951. Rows of mature shelter trees outline the fairways, encouraging straight tee shots, and the small, well-kept greens demand precision.

name: Green Acres Country Club
description: An 18-hole course in West Plains, only ten minutes from Invercargill city centre. The accessible layout and proximity to town make it a convenient option for visitors wanting a full round in Southland.

name: Mataura Golf Club
description: A flat, tree-lined 9-hole course five minutes south of the township of Mataura. Established in 1974, it uses alternate tees for the back nine to create a full 18-hole experience through attractive Southland farmland.

name: Nightcaps Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course nestled under the Takitimu Mountains in the former coal-mining town of Nightcaps. The undulating terrain provides an interesting and testing layout with a distinctly rural Western Southland character.

name: Ringa Ringa Heights Golf Club
description: A unique 6-hole course on Stewart Island, reached by ferry across the Foveaux Strait from Bluff. Surrounded by native bush and ocean views, it offers one of the most remote and adventurous golfing experiences in New Zealand.

name: Tokanui Golf Club
description: New Zealand's southernmost mainland golf course, a treeless links-style 9-hole perched above the Southern Ocean near Fortrose on the Catlins coast. Wind and sea views of the Mataura River estuary define every round at this exposed, character-filled layout.

name: Tuatapere Golf Club
description: A flat parkland course in the Western Southland town of Tuatapere, nestled close to bush-clad limestone cliffs on a former racecourse. The club recently celebrated its centenary, and the well-maintained layout is regarded as one of the best 9-hole courses in Southland.

name: Waikaia Golf Club
description: Often called the jewel of Southland golf, this picturesque 9-hole course features a signature river hole where brown trout can be spotted feeding below. The peaceful Northern Southland setting makes it a hidden gem well worth seeking out.

name: Hastings Golf Club
description: A long-established club set in the orchard country of Hastings, offering a well-maintained parkland layout in the heart of Hawke's Bay. The mature tree-lined fairways and pleasant surroundings make for an enjoyable round in one of New Zealand's premier fruit-growing regions.

name: Ardleigh Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course near Palmerston in Otago.

name: Belleknowes Golf Club
description: A friendly club in the heart of Dunedin with spectacular views of the city, harbour and out to sea. Surrounded by one of only three Victorian botanic gardens in the southern hemisphere.

name: Maniototo Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course in Ranfurly in the Maniototo plains of Central Otago.

name: St Clair Golf Club
description: A championship 18-hole course with world-class sea views. Signature hole 15 sits right on the coastline, a popular photo spot.

name: Twelve Oaks Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course near Mosgiel in the Taieri Plains.

name: Waitoa Park Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course in the Deborah area near Oamaru.

name: Heriot Golf Club
description: A picturesque 9-hole course in the heart of West Otago, featuring well-groomed greens and gently rolling fairways lined with mature trees. The friendly rural club welcomes visitors to this quiet corner of the Otago countryside.

name: Kaitangata Golf Club
description: A beginner-friendly 9-hole course in South Otago, set alongside Wangaloa Beach just 20 minutes from Balclutha. The coastal setting and welcoming club atmosphere make it a relaxed spot for a casual round.

name: Lake Hawea  Golf Club
description: A relaxed, family-friendly 9-hole course near Albert Town, just ten minutes from Wanaka. Built in 2001 near the shores of Lake Hawea, the course welcomes casual drop-in play with no tee-time bookings required.

name: Lower Waitaki Golf Club
description: A welcoming par-72 course on the flat plains near the mouth of the Waitaki River, 12 km north of Oamaru. Easy-flowing greens and well-tended fairways make it a pleasant round, and the friendly membership adds to the experience.

name: Omarama Golf Club
description: A pleasant, flat 9-hole course in the "place of light," bounded by the Omarama Stream with fine mountain views in every direction. The clever clover-leaf design brings players past the clubhouse every three holes, perfectly placed for a refreshment stop on a Central Otago summer day.

name: Owaka Golf Club
description: A 9-hole course along the banks of the Owaka River in the Catlins, surrounded by lush Otago countryside. The remote southern location and peaceful setting make it an appealing detour for golfers exploring the Catlins coast.

name: Taieri Lakes Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course at the base of Three Mile Hill in North Taieri, just 15 minutes from central Dunedin. The layout makes good use of the surrounding lake and hill terrain to create an engaging round close to the city.

name: Tapanui Golf Club
description: An 18-hole course on the northern edge of Tapanui in West Otago, featuring a newly refurbished clubhouse. The rural setting along State Highway 90 provides a pleasant backdrop for a full round in this quiet farming district.

name: Tokarahi Golf Club
description: A beautifully maintained 9-hole course in the Maerewhenua Valley of North Otago, climbing to 280 metres above sea level. From the upper holes, panoramic views stretch across to the Kakanui Mountains, St Marys Range, and the Waitaki Valley.

name: Queens Park Golf Club
